description: Reasoning vault aligned with OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §4.1: represent linear functions, interpret slope as constant rate of change, graph and write equations, and compare parallel and perpendicular lines.

archetypes.name: Read a Linear Function Representation
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §4.1 — Representing Linear Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: A linear function has a constant rate of change and can be represented consistently by a rule, table, graph, or ordered pairs.
archetypes.mentalModel: The slope describes the repeated vertical change for each horizontal step; the intercept anchors the graph where the input is zero.

cognitiveTraps.description: Reversing the order of output differences but not input differences when computing slope.
Treating the vertical intercept as the rate of change or reading the coefficient of x as the intercept.
Dropping a negative sign when the output decreases as the input increases.

figureBuilders.title: A linear function has a constant slope and a y-intercept

archetypes.name: Write a Line from a Point and Slope
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §4.1 — Writing Equations of Lines
archetypes.coreConcept: A slope and one point determine exactly one line; substituting the point into point-slope form determines its equation.
archetypes.mentalModel: Use the point as an anchor and the slope as the line's fixed step pattern.

cognitiveTraps.description: Mishandling a negative point coordinate inside the point-slope expression.
Changing the sign of a point coordinate incorrectly while isolating the intercept.

archetypes.figureNone: The requested skill is symbolic construction from a stated slope and point; a graph adds no information needed to determine the equation.

archetypes.name: Determine Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §4.1 — Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
archetypes.coreConcept: Distinct nonvertical parallel lines share a slope; nonvertical perpendicular lines have slopes whose product is -1.
archetypes.mentalModel: Parallel lines preserve the same step pattern; perpendicular step patterns are negative reciprocals.

cognitiveTraps.description: Taking a reciprocal without changing its sign when finding a perpendicular slope.
Assigning a negative reciprocal to a parallel line instead of keeping the same slope.

archetypes.figureNone: The slope rules directly classify the line relationship; a diagram is not needed for the symbolic task.

archetypes.name: Diagnose a Slope or Intercept Error
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §4.1 — Interpreting Slope and Linear Equations
archetypes.coreConcept: A proposed linear rule must preserve both its rate of change and its value at the stated input.
archetypes.mentalModel: Check the proposed line against its defining data: the slope pattern and at least one anchor point.

cognitiveTraps.description: Swapping the slope and y-intercept when reading or writing slope-intercept form.
Using inconsistent subtraction order in the numerator and denominator of the slope formula.

archetypes.figureNone: The item asks for a symbolic first-error diagnosis from a short derivation; a plot is unnecessary and would not improve the diagnosis.
